name: Germanicus Caesar
bio: Germanicus Caesar is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no firm date for the poet. Paton's index lists him as Germanicus Caesar.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 17, 18).

poems.title: Book IX, 17
poems.author: Germanicus Caesar
poems.text: Once a hare from the mountain height leapt into the sea in her effort to escape from a dog’s cruel fangs. But not even thus did she escape her fate ; for at once a sea-dog seized her and bereft her of life. Out of the fire, as the saying is, into the flame didst thou fall. Of a truth Fate reared thee to be a meal for a dog either on the land or in the sea.

poems.title: Book IX, 18: On the Same
poems.author: Germanicus Caesar
poems.text: One dog captured me after another. What is strange in that? Beasts of the water and beasts of the land have like rage against me. Henceforth, ye hares, may the sky be open to your course. But I fear thee, Heaven; thou too hast a dog among thy stars. II
